html:
Saba was the leading kingdom of ancient Yemen, with its capital at Marib, from at least the 8th century BCE until it was absorbed by Himyar around 275 CE. It is the Sheba of the Bible and the Quran.

Saba grew rich on the incense trade, sending frankincense and myrrh north by camel to the Mediterranean. Its rulers built the Marib Dam and great temples, and wrote in the South Arabian script. The legend of the Queen of Sheba and her visit to Solomon is still told in Yemen and Ethiopia.

Saba competed with neighbouring kingdoms such as Qataban and Hadhramaut, and in the end lost out to Himyar, which united the south.
